content:
## How many people can ride in a hot air balloon in Cappadocia?

It depends on the basket: from a private basket for a couple or small group to large shared baskets with many passengers. A balloon is limited by weight rather than a fixed headcount, and the pilot confirms the load on the morning. Trip and Tick's Standard shared flight starts from €100 per person.

If you have looked at photographs of a Cappadocia sunrise, you have already seen the range without noticing it. Small, deep baskets drift close to the fairy chimneys while wide, partitioned ones carry a row of passengers along the rim. They fly the same valleys at the same hour; they are simply different aircraft. Operators usually describe them as private, comfort or standard flights.

We give no single passenger number here because it is not standardised: it changes by operator, envelope size and basket design. Ask for the stated number of passengers for your flight rather than relying on the label on a web page.

## What actually limits the number of passengers?

Lift comes from the difference between the hot air inside the envelope and the colder air outside, so what a balloon can carry changes with temperature, altitude and fuel load. The aircraft has a maximum take-off weight, and the pilot checks the passenger load against it before the flight.

A larger envelope holds more heated air and lifts more, which is why the biggest baskets hang beneath the biggest envelopes. Air temperature matters too. The Nevşehir weather station's 1981–2010 averages run from a January maximum of 4.1 °C to a July maximum of 29.3 °C. In cold air the same balloon can lift more, and on a warm morning a pilot may fly with fewer passengers or less fuel to stay inside the weight limit.

Commercial ballooning in Turkey is regulated by the civil aviation authority (SHGM). For comparison, the EU publishes its own rules for balloon operations as Commission Regulation (EU) 2018/395 on the EASA website; treat that as a reference for what such rules cover, not as proof of what a given Turkish operator follows. Passenger numbers sit inside these rules; they are not a marketing decision.

## Standard, comfort and private flights

Operators generally sell some mix of three formats. A private flight takes a couple or a small group, a comfort or small-group flight takes a limited group, and a standard flight takes the largest number of passengers sharing one basket. The wording is not standardised between companies, so ask what the label means for the company you are booking with.

| Format | What you can expect | What it feels like |
|---|---|---|
| Private / romantic | The basket is for your group only | The pilot flies with your group alone; Trip and Tick quotes this on request |
| Comfort / small group | A limited group | More room to move and an easier view over the rim |
| Standard shared | The largest numbers | More people around you; the most widely sold option, from €100 per person with Trip and Tick |

Larger commercial baskets are usually divided into compartments, with the pilot and fuel cylinders in the middle. That layout lets many passengers stand in their own section for the whole flight, so nobody has to move while the balloon is climbing or landing.

## Does a smaller basket give you a better flight?

Not a different flight, but a different experience. Every balloon that lifts off around Göreme on a given morning follows the same wind over the same valleys, so the landscape is the same. What changes with a smaller basket is elbow room, an uninterrupted view over the rim, and how much of the pilot's attention you get.

For photographers this matters more than it sounds. In a full shared basket you share one side of a compartment, so you shoot in one general direction and wait for the balloon to rotate. In a smaller basket you can step and change your framing. For most first-time visitors a standard shared flight delivers the sunrise they came for, at a fraction of the cost of chartering the whole aircraft.

## Children, height and who counts as a passenger

Children count as full passengers: they take up weight and space like anyone else. Trip and Tick does not accept children under 6, and children aged 7-12 pay 80% of the adult price. Other operators set their own minimum age, so ask before you book.

There are no seats in a balloon basket, so everyone stands for the entire flight and has to climb in over the basket wall unaided. Rim height varies between baskets, so a small child may see mostly basket wall; ask about it before you book rather than at the launch field in the dark. Pregnant travellers and people who cannot stand unsupported for the flight are not accepted on our flights; that is a safety rule rather than a preference.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can I book a whole balloon for my group?**
Yes. A private flight means you have the basket to your group only, so the price covers the aircraft rather than a seat. Trip and Tick quotes private flights on request via WhatsApp.

**Can the number of passengers change on the day?**
It can. The pilot checks weight against air temperature and fuel load and may fly with fewer people than the maximum. Flights also depend on the weather, so every booking is conditional on wind and visibility.

**Do all the passengers stand together in one open space?**
Not usually in a large basket. Larger commercial baskets are normally divided into compartments around a central pilot area, and you stay in your own compartment for the flight.

**What is the youngest age Trip and Tick accepts?**
Children must be at least 6. Children aged 7-12 pay 80% of the adult price, and children under 6 are not permitted for safety reasons.

Check live availability and prices for the flight type you want at tripandtick.com.
